title: Adaptive time-decay batch credits for per-vector pricing (rerank pilot)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood customers running large rerank pipelines have spiky per-vector volume (short bursts of heavy traffic for index rebuilds, search re-ranks, and large batch rerank jobs). Current per-vector unit pricing plus a static batch discount tier causes two problems: (1) teams either over-commit capacity to avoid cost predictability issues during spikes or (2) they pay high marginal costs for short bursts. The goal of this ticket is to prototype an adaptive "time-decay" batch-credit system that awards temporary per-vector credits based on recent sustained activity, aligning short-term economics to workload reality while limiting long-tail exposure for Redwood and keeping contract language simple for enterprise QSA/QSA reviewers.

Goal:
- Build and test a pricing experiment that provides transient batch credits for rerank-heavy customers using a sliding time window and exponential decay.
- Measure customer cost delta, platform revenue delta, and behavioral effects (deferred batch scheduling, traffic smoothing).
- Produce QSA-ready contract language and SOW appendix describing credit logic, auditability, and controls.

Success metrics (30d experiment):
- Revenue impact: within -5% to +10% relative to baseline for qualified pilot customers (no large negative revenue surprise).
- Customer satisfaction: pilot customers report perceived cost-stability improvement in post-pilot survey (NPS delta > +5).
- Behavior: >= 20% of eligible burst events use credit smoothing vs. baseline scheduling.
- Ops: No more than 1 spike-related billing dispute in pilot cohort.

Design summary:
- Eligibility: Customers enrolled in rerank/embeddings enterprise plans (explicit opt-in).
- Credit model: For each customer, compute a rolling 24-hour weighted sum of per-vector usage where more recent tokens are weighted higher (exponential decay half-life configurable, default 6 hours). When the rolling sum crosses a per-vector threshold, issue "transient credits" that cover a portion of per-vector unit charges for the subsequent 6 hours. Credits scale with the delta over baseline sustained usage rather than absolute volume to discourage gaming.
- Cap & reconciliation: Per-customer monthly cap (configurable, default $5k) and audit log for each credit issuance with cause and decay curve. Credits are reconciled daily and appear as line-items in billing exports for transparency.
- Pricing knobs to experiment with: decay half-life (4h/6h/12h), credit coverage (50%/75%/90%), issuance threshold (% above baseline: 50%/100%/200%), and monthly cap.

Contract/QSA considerations:
- We need a short appendix describing the deterministic algorithm, data sources (token counts per-request, timestamps), replayability for audits, and which billing exports to use for third-party verification.
- Security notes: credit logic uses aggregated usage metrics and not raw prompt text. Still need to confirm that aggregated telemetry in billing exports meets customer data-handling requirements.
- Legal/Finance: propose clause for pilot customers: "Pilot pricing adjustments are temporary and reflected in monthly invoices; Redwood reserves right to terminate pilot with 30 days' notice." Ask Legal to confirm acceptable language.

Experiment plan (weeks):
- Week 0 (now): finalize algorithm and config defaults; create design doc and QSA appendix draft.
- Week 1: engineering spike to implement issuance engine and billing export hooks (ENG-19872). Build simulation harness to replay 3 months of historical rerank traffic and produce expected credit issuance.
- Week 2: run simulation on 10 representative customers, present delta to finance, adjust knobs.
- Week 3-6: run live pilot with 8 customers (opt-in), monitor metrics and billing reconciliation daily.
- Week 7: compile results, prepare roll/no-roll recommendation and QSA/contract language for wider availability.

Measurement & instrumentation:
- New telemetry: credit_issued_event (customer, timestamp, amount, cause_tag), credit_balance per-customer, billing_line_items flagged as "transient_credit".
- Dashboards: per-customer credit issuance rate, cost delta, disputes, top customers by credits.
- CRO baseline replay: run simulation to estimate worst-case exposure and compare to monthly cap; provide finance with 99th percentile exposure numbers.

Risks & mitigations:
- Gaming: Customers could artificially inflate traffic to obtain credits. Mitigation: credits scale to delta over baseline and include anomaly detection (sudden non-human patterns flagged for manual review).
- Complexity in contract/QSA: Keep appendix deterministic, emphasize aggregated inputs, and limit pilot to opt-in customers with standard audit access.
- Billing reconciliation errors: Build a daily reconciliation job and manual fallbacks for disputes.

Deliverables:
- Design doc + QSA appendix (Confluence link)
- Simulation harness + replay results (GitHub PR link)
- Billing export line-item implementation and dashboard (Console change request)
- Pilot recruitment list and customer comms template

Next steps / To do:
- [PM] Finalize QSA appendix and loop Legal (Aisha) — by 2026-03-05.
- [ENG] Prototype issuance engine and simulation (ENG-19872) — start 2026-03-02.
- [Finance] Provide expected revenue sensitivity thresholds and sign-off for monthly cap range.
- [Design] Create simple customer-facing one-pager explaining credits and examples for pilot customers.
